reference_items.subject: Advanced Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
For what real value of k will the equation below describe a circle with radius 3?

x^2 + y^2 + 2x - 4y + k = 0

Show all your work.

descriptors:
K = -4. Method used:
• Because of the quadratic and linear terms, the equation must be of the general form (x+1)^2 + (y-2)^2 . From that we get the equation
• (x+1)^2 + (y-2)^2 -5 + k = 0
• (x+1)^2 +(y-2)^2 = 5 - k
• If the radius is 3, right hand side must equal 9 (= r^2)
• Hence 5 - k = 9 and k = -4 is the only solution.

k = -4. Method used:
• All circles with radius 3 have same general form: x^2 + y^2 - 2ax - 2by + a^2 + b^2 - 9 = 0.
• From that: 2 = -2a; -4 = -2b; k = a^2+b^2 -9;
• Hence a = -1, b = 2, k = -4.
Any other fully correct solution.
k = -4. No work shown.
Method as in code 20 but with numerical error(s) only.
Method as in code 21 but with numerical error(s) only.
All other partially correct solutions.
Incorrect answer. No work shown.

k = -12 with or without work shown.
[This answer can be obtained by the misconception that point (3,3) is on the circle, hence x = 3 and y = 3 are put into the equation.]

k = 3 OR k = 9 OR k = -9 with or without work shown.
[This answer can be obtained by the miscoknception that the parameter k represents the radius or square of radius of the circle.]

k = 8 or k = 2 or k = 14 with or without work shown.
[This answer can be obtained by the misconception that -5 + k = 3 OR 5 - k = 3 OR -5 + k = 9.]
All other incorrect responses with some work shown.
Crossed-out, illegible, or impossible to interpret.
BLANK

reference_items.subject: Advanced Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Find all real values of x which satisfy the following equation:

sqrt(x) - 2/sqrt(x) = 1

Show all your work.

descriptors:
x = 4. Method:
1. Original equation transformed to quadratic equation, x^2 - 5x + 4 = 0.
2. Two roots, x=4 and x=1 found and checked in original equation.
3. x=1 is rejected as a solution of the original equation; x=4 is accepted.
Note: Since the original equation is squared, it is necessary to check both roots in the original equation.

x = 4. Method:
1. Substitution (e.g., sqrt(x) = a) used and the original equation transformed, without squaring, into the quadratic equation a^2 - a - 2 = 0.
2. Two roots found, a = 2 and a = -1.
3. a = -1 rejected since a = -1 ≠ sqrt(x) , sqrt(x) ≥ 0 .
4. By substitution reversed.a = 2 implies sqrt(x) = 2, thus x = 4. Checking in original equation is not necessary.

x = 4. Method:
1. Graphs y = sqrt(x) - 2/sqrt(x) - 1 for x > 0 correctly.
2. x-coordinate of y-intercept is found to be 4.
3. Justifies that graph is increasing and thus x = 4 is an unique solution.
4. x = 4 is checked in original equation.
Other completely correct solutions.
Uses code 30 to find x = 4 and x = 1 and states both are roots.
Uses code 31 to find a = 2 and a = -1 and then either goes no further or makes an incorrect statement such as 4 and 1 or 2 and 1 are roots of the original equation.
Uses code 32 showing graph, states x = 4 is a root and x = 4 is checked in the original equation.
Other solutions with correct overall method but with minor error(s).
x = 4. No work shown or some work shown, such as checking x = 4 in original equation but no argument given for why there are no other roots.
Solution as in codes 30 or 31: Original equation is transformed correctly into a quadratic equation, by any method, but quadratic equation either is not solved or incorrectly solved.
Solution as in code 22 (graphical) except that except that x = 4 is NOT checked in original equation.
Other minimally correct or incomplete solutions such as a simplification of the equation to x - 2 = sqrt(x) .
Solution as in codes 30 or 31 except original equation is transformed into an incorrect quadratic equation or to a non-quadratic equation.
Other incorrect responses.
Crossed-out, illegible, or impossible to interpret.

reference_items.stem: The graph of the function g passes through the point (1,2). The slope of the tangent to the graph at any point (x, y) is given by g'(x) = 6x − 12. What is g(x)? Show all your work.

descriptors: g(x) = 3x^2 - 12x + 11. Method: First the function g is determined to be of the form g(x) = 3x^2 - 12 x + c. Then c is found to be 11 by solving the equation g(1) = 2, i.e. 3 - 12 + c = 2.
g(x) = 3x^2 - 12x + 11. Other correct method used.
g(x) = 3x^2 - 12 x + 11. No work shown.

Answer of the form g(x) = 3 x^2 - 12 x + c, where c is a numerical value other than 11. Method correct; the value of c given incorrectly due to error in solving the equation g(1) = 2. If c = 13, check to determine if 13 results from an error in solving g(1) = 2[code 21] or from solving correctly the "reversed" equation, g(2) = 1 [code 22].
Method: Solves the "reversed" equation g(2) = 1 and determines the value of c to be 13. If an error is made in solving the reversed equation; c determined to be a number other than 13, use code 11.
Answers of the form g(x) = 3x^2 -12x + c, where the value of c is NOT determined by solving either g(1) = 2 or g(2) = 1.
Other nearly complete solutions with a minor error.

Method: Incorrectly solves "reversed" equation g(2) = 1, finds c to be a number other than 13.

reference_items.subject: Advanced Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
A function f is defined by:

f(x) = −x − 1   if   −2 < x ≤ −1
f(x) = x + 1   if   −1 < x ≤ 0
f(x) = −x + 1   if   0 < x ≤ 1
f(x) = x − 1   if   1 < x ≤ 2

Which is the graph of f?
reference_items.figure_description:
Each option shows a Cartesian coordinate system with a horizontal x-axis and a vertical f(x)-axis.

Option A: The x-axis has tick marks labeled −2, −1, 0, 1, 2. The f(x)-axis has a tick mark labeled 1. A continuous V-shaped wave is drawn: it starts with an open circle at (−2, 1), goes down to (−1, 0), up to (0, 1), down to (1, 0), and up to a solid dot at (2, 1).

Option B: The x-axis has tick marks labeled −2, −1, 0, 1, 2. The f(x)-axis has a tick mark labeled 1. A continuous wave is drawn: it starts with an open circle at (−2, 0), goes up to (−1, 1), down to (0, 0), up to (1, 1), and down to a solid dot at (2, 0).

Option C: The x-axis has tick marks labeled −2, −1, 0, 1, 2. The f(x)-axis has a tick mark labeled 1. Four parallel line segments of slope −1 are drawn: one from an open circle at (−2, 1) to a solid dot at (−1, 0); one from an open circle at (−1, 1) to a solid dot at (0, 0); one from an open circle at (0, 1) to a solid dot at (1, 0); and one from an open circle at (1, 1) to a solid dot at (2, 0).

Option D: The horizontal axis is labeled x with a tick mark at 1. The vertical axis is labeled f(x) with tick marks labeled −2, −1, 0, 1, 2. A continuous zigzag path is drawn from an open circle at (1, 2) to (0, 1), then to (1, 0), then to (0, −1), and ending at a solid dot at (1, −2).

Option E: The x-axis has tick marks labeled −2, −1, 0, 1, 2. The f(x)-axis has tick marks labeled −1 and 1. Four separate line segments are drawn: from an open circle at (−2, 0) down to a solid dot at (−1, −1); from an open circle at (−1, 0) up to a solid dot at (0, 1); from an open circle at (0, 0) down to a solid dot at (1, −1); and from an open circle at (1, 0) up to a solid dot at (2, 1).
